results.title: About | LokFeel
results.visibleText: LokFee! Pricing About Log in Get Started AGENT-NATIVE CONNECTION OS About LokFeel An agent-native workspace for teams and communities to coordinate connections, approvals, and measurable outcomes. Why we built it Most work starts as a sentence and dies in a thread. Someone says what they want, a model answers, and three days later nobody can reconstruct what was decided, who approved it, or whether it happened. LokFeel exists to close that gap. The unit of work is not a message — it is a compiled workspace: a goal, its constraints, the people involved, the boundaries they agreed to, and the outcome that can be checked afterwards. That means the interesting engineering is not the chat box. It is the compiler, the permission model, and the reconciliation trail. Everything else is interface. What LokFeel is A compiler from plain-language intent to a validated workspace spec A consent layer that gates fields and actions, enforced server-side An outcome ledger where every number traces back to an event An open surface: MCP tools, A2A tasks, a published OpenAPI contract What it is not Not a chatbot wrapper — a run that produces no spec or mission is a failure Not a general low-code canvas — fields are whitelisted, not free-form Not an autonomous agent that acts without approval Not a single-player tool — workspaces belong to an organization How a run works Four stages, each one inspectable. results.title: FAQ | LokFeel
results.visibleText: LokFee! Pricing About Log in Get Started Frequently Asked Questions How LokFeel works, and where its limits are What is LokFeel? LokFeel is an Agent-Native Connection OS. You describe an outcome in plain language; the system compiles it into a structured, schema-validated workspace containing the goal, its constraints, the people involved, the boundaries they approve, and the metrics that define success. Work happens inside that workspace — not in a chat thread that disappears. What happens when I describe a goal? A run goes through four stages: Intent is captured, a workspace spec is compiled and validated, consent gates are applied to fields and actions, and outcomes are recorded and reconciled. If a stage cannot be verified, the run does not advance — a failed compilation is shown as failed, never as success. What can the AI actually change — and what needs approval? The model proposes; it does not execute. It can produce a draft spec, suggest candidates and recommend a next step, but every write that touches people or money passes a server-side permission check and, where the spec requires it, an explicit approval. Sensitive actions with no valid consent are rejected by the API, not hidden in the UI. Who is LokFeel for? Teams and communities that coordinate work involving other people: recruiting, partnerships, member introductions, vendor onboarding, internal approvals. If your work currently lives in threads and spreadsheets, and you need to know who approved what, it fits. How is my organization's data isolated?
